NUM	<p>b796_8eb4</p> <h4>Three-Point Test Cross Problem</h4><p>A test cross is a way to explore the relationship between genes and their respective alleles. It is a useful tool for genetic mapping and deciphering the inheritance of traits. Specifically, a three-point test cross examines three (3) genes at the same time to learn about their assortment in gamete formation.</p><p>A standard three-point test cross involves crossing a heterozygous organism for all three genes with an organism that is homozygous recessive for all three genes</p> <p>For this problem, a test cross using a fruit fly (<i>Drosophila melanogaster</i>) heterozygous for three genes was conducted to understand their genetic interactions.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9c3a1c;">Gene N</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9c3a1c;"><i>nerdy</i></span>' phenotype. A fruit fly that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c3a1c;">Gene N</span> has large, prominent eyes that stand out, much like thick-rimmed glasses.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c68;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006c68;"><i>prickly</i></span>' phenotype. A fruit fly that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c68;">Gene P</span> is covered with sharp bristles, giving it a spiky texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4550bd;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4550bd;"><i>tipsy</i></span>' phenotype. A fruit fly that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4550bd;">Gene T</span> moves in an erratic path, suggesting a lack of coordination, as if intoxicated.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse;
